verdicts.title: The Bidirected Cut Relaxation for Steiner Tree has Integrality Gap Smaller Than 2
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The Steiner tree problem is one of the most prominent problems in network design. Given an edge-weighted undirected graph and a subset of the vertices, called terminals, the task is to compute a minimum-weight tree containing all terminals (and possibly further vertices). The best-known approximation algorithms for Steiner tree involve enumeration of a (polynomial but) very large number of candidate components and are therefore slow in practice.
